question: The shehnai is a reed instrument with how many holes along the tube?
solution:
The correct answer is **Seven**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Shehnai:

 
 
• It is a reed instrument in which there are seven holes along the tube which are used for playing the melody by opening and closing them with the fingers.
 
• It is known as a Mangal vadya and is usually played on all auspicious occasions in north India such as marriages, temple festivals, etc.
 
• The Shehnai is considered to have come to India from West Asia, there are other scholars who believe that this instrument travelled to China from India.
 
• It is now a popular instrument in concerts, the sound is very sweet and suited for playing Raga Sangeet.
 
• In the early fifties of this century, Ustad Bismillah Khan is credited for popularizing this instrument.
 
• Today, Pt. Anant Lal and Pt. Daya Shankar are also noted Shehnai players.
